sections.text:
2 Peter is written as a reminder from someone who knows he will soon die. It urges believers to grow in goodness, knowledge and love, and appeals to what the apostles saw of Jesus’ glory.

The middle chapter warns against teachers who promise freedom while living for themselves. The last chapter answers people who scoff that the Lord has not returned: God is patient, not slow, and wants people to turn to him.

The letter presents itself as written by Peter. Its authorship is the most disputed in the New Testament, mainly because its style differs from 1 Peter and its second chapter closely matches the letter of Jude. It speaks of Paul’s letters as already well known.

The description of the heavens and the earth being dissolved by fire (3:10 to 13) is read by some as the destruction of the present world and by others as its purifying and renewal. Either way the letter turns the expectation into a question about how to live now.
